commit.message:
feat: JWT revocation via token_version + admin user management (Issue #60)

- users.token_version column (alembic revision a003_user_token_version)
- create_access_token embeds 'ver' claim; get_current_user rejects stale
  versions -> demotion/revocation takes effect on the NEXT request, not
  after 8h token expiry
- New admin endpoints (RBAC Admin-only, audit-logged):
  - GET  /auth/users                      (list accounts)
  - POST /auth/users/{u}/revoke-tokens     (kill all outstanding JWTs)
  - POST /auth/users/{u}/role?new_role=X   (role change + auto-revocation)
  Guards: invalid roles 400, self-demotion 400, non-admin 403.
- Login/signup issue tokens bound to the current token_version.
- tests/test_token_revocation.py: 7 regression tests (all passing) —
  ver claim present, revocation kills old token + fresh login works,
  role change revokes + reflects new role, guards enforced, out-of-band
  bump kills minted token.

Closes #60

feat(security): session revocation + streaming body cap (audit G06/G07)

G06 — a signed JWT alone is no longer a session: resolve_session() checks the
live account (exists, active) and the token's version against
users.token_version on every request, so logout, password change, env-driven
password reset, role edits and deactivation take effect immediately.
- new users.token_version column + migration f8b9c0d1e2f3
- POST /auth/logout revokes all issued tokens (bump + audit event)
- change-password returns a replacement token and revokes the old ones
- SSE stream resolves the same live session
- role now comes from the DB row, not the token claim

G07 — BodySizeLimitMiddleware caps actually received bytes (chunked bodies
without Content-Length included); answers 413 itself because FastAPI turns
body-read exceptions into 400s. Covers early-return routes (login, webhooks).

Tests: revoked/inactive/role-change/logout/password-rotation + chunked and
oversized bodies (346 passed, 1 skipped).

commit.message:
Re-read the user on refresh and on every request; revoke tokens by version

Refresh loads the user from the control DB: refused when they're gone or
their token version moved on, takes the role from the database, and keeps
the refresh_exp set at login (no sliding). A token refreshes once (atomic
revoke). users.token_version (control migration 3f9c1d2e7a64) is in every
JWT as tv; changing a role or resetting a password bumps it, deleting the
user removes the row, and the middleware refuses a token that doesn't
match, taking the role from the database.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(auth): add regression tests for JWT revocation

Covers Finding 8 (CWE-613):
- issued tokens carry the user's token version ("tv")
- a token is rejected with 401 "Session has been revoked" after logout
- logout on one device revokes tokens on every device
- the next login issues a working token with the new version
- an admin role change revokes old tokens; after logging in again the
  user gets the new role
- deactivate then reactivate does not bring old tokens back
- tokenVersion never appears in API responses
- tokens signed with HS512 or "none" are rejected (algorithm pinning)

fix(auth): revoke access tokens on password change, single-use email verification, MFA verify rate limit, admin role versioning (#77 #79 #80 #81 #97 #98 #99 #100 #101)

- User.auth_version column; access tokens carry 'av' claim; auth-service
  boundaries reject tokens minted before the last credential rotation
  (password change bumps the version; refresh tokens already revoked)
- Email-verification tokens consumed exactly once via atomic blacklist
  insert; replay and concurrent use rejected; new resend after verify
  issues nothing (enumeration-safe)
- /auth/mfa/login-verify rate-limited per IP (30/15min) and per user
  (10/15min), fail-open on Redis outage
- Access tokens carry 'arv' admin role version; content/search/moderation/
  admin admin gates compare against their ADMIN_ROLE_VERSION setting so
  revoking an admin from ADMIN_EMAILS (bump version) is immediate
- DB: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN auth_version (live dev stack applied)
- Live-verified: stale access token 401 right after password change,
  fresh token works (av=1), verification token replay 400
- Tests: auth 168 (+7), content 93, search 57, moderation 36, admin 74

Revoke sessions immediately on deactivation, role change, password change and logout

Tokens used to be trusted until they expired (up to 10h), and the roles
inside them were never re-checked. So a disabled or demoted user kept
their access, and logging out only cleared the browser's copy.

- Add users.token_version (V5) and put it in the JWT as the "tv" claim
- The JWT filter loads the user on every request and rejects the token if
  the user is missing, inactive, or the version doesn't match; roles now
  come from the database instead of the token
- Bump token_version on deactivation, role change, and admin or
  self-service password change
- Add POST /api/auth/logout, which revokes every token the user has
- Frontend: logout calls the endpoint; a self password change signs the
  user out and sends them to the login page
- Add regression tests for F-04

Existing tokens have no version and are rejected, so all users must
sign in again once after deploy. V5 must be applied by hand

feat(auth): revocable sessions and user management

Tokens were stateless 7-day JWTs with no way to revoke them, and there was no
API to delete a user or change a role.

- Users have a tokenVersion (migration 0003); tokens carry it as 'tv'. Every
  authenticated request (REST, WebSocket feed, media proxy) checks that the user
  still exists, has the same role and the same token version (10s cache,
  invalidated on change). Tokens issued before this change count as version 0,
  so the upgrade logs nobody out.
- New endpoints (audited): PATCH /api/auth/users/:id (role), DELETE
  /api/auth/users/:id, POST /api/auth/users/:id/reset-password, POST
  /api/auth/users/:id/revoke-sessions (admin or self), POST /api/auth/me/password
  (returns a fresh token). Role changes and password resets revoke the user's
  sessions; admins cannot delete or demote themselves or the last admin.
- The first-boot wizard revokes every session opened with the factory password
  and hands the installer a new token.
- UI: role, password reset, sign-out-everywhere and delete in user management;
  a 'My account' card in Settings to change your own password or sign out
  everywhere.
- Tests sign tokens through a helper that creates the user, so they run the real
  session check instead of a test bypass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01G6LNQAXwNL8i1Q3s3mSsoo

feat(access): admin-only role and permission management

Add /api/admin roles + permissions endpoints (AdminOnly) to create roles and
grant/revoke permissions. Role assignment to users is now Admin-only (it let any
users.manage holder promote themselves to Admin). Role/permission changes bump
token version and revoke refresh tokens so they apply immediately. The Admin
role is immutable and the last active Admin can not lose it. New migration
ensures the permission catalog and Admin role exist when the dev seed is off.

commit.message:
fix(api): make role and email changes credentials changes, and normalise emails (#503, #504)

Role change (#504). UpdateRolesAsync writes the level and raises
CredentialsVersion in one statement, then revokes every refresh token
and personal access token in the same transaction, and publishes the
account on world:accounts:disconnect, best-effort. A promotion does the
same: only a new login gets the new roles onto the TCP session. The
admin is recorded as the revoker (new actorId parameter).

Email (#503).
- Emails are stored trimmed and with the whole address lower-cased
  (AccountEmail.Normalise); FindByEmailAsync normalises its input.
  Accounts.Email gets a unique index and a check constraint. The
  migration refuses to run, naming the accounts, on normalised
  duplicates or unnormalised rows, and changes nothing.
- Registration and the start of an email change refuse a taken address
  as "Email already exists", including a registration or a confirm that
  loses the race to the index.
- Starting an email change needs the current password
  (IReauthentication); the pending change records the credentials
  version it was proved at.
- Confirming it writes the email with a version bump, compare-and-set on
  that version, revokes every refresh token and PAT in the same
  transaction, and publishes the disconnect.

The confirm token is still not delivered: the API has no email sender.

OPE-1366: end stale sessions — session_version for web JWTs + refresh-time re-check for MCP OAuth grants (#1608)

Web (AUTH4): the jwt callback now stamps users.session_version + checkedAt at
sign-in and re-reads {role, roles, session_version} from D1 at most every
5 minutes. A deleted user or a changed version returns null (Auth.js core
0.41 clears the cookie); otherwise role/roles are refreshed. D1 failure is
fail-open (token kept, checkedAt not advanced, logged).

session_version (drizzle/0371, default 0) is bumped on an admin role change
(PATCH /api/admin/users/[id]) and on password reset success.

MCP (AUTH5): a tokenExchangeCallback re-resolves props via resolveUserProps on
refresh; a missing user or changed session_version throws invalid_grant (the
provider revokes the grant); a D1 error answers 503 temporarily_unavailable
without revoking. Login now stamps sessionVersion into props. Max MCP
staleness = the default 1 h access-token TTL.

Co-authored-by: John Tarbox <JohnTarbox@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Add JWT token version revocation support

Implement server-side JWT invalidation using a new `users.token_version` column (Flyway V14) and propagate it through user models, mappers, principals, and token claims. The auth filter now cross-checks token claims against current DB state (active status, token version, and role consistency) so deactivated users, stale tokens, and role-contradicting tokens are rejected. Adds `/api/auth/logout` to revoke active sessions, increments token version on deactivation/provisioning/role updates, records new audit events for token revocation and role changes, updates seed data, and expands security tests to cover these revocation and authorization scenarios.

commit.message:
docs: embed effective roles in access-token claims, revoke via token_version

Reverse the earlier decision to always re-resolve RoleAssignment/team
membership from the DB per request. Access tokens now carry a roles
claim (flattened snapshot of direct + team-inherited grants) and a tv
claim (User.token_version at issuance), closer to how Keycloak embeds
roles. Authorization middleware reads roles straight from the token
instead of joining role_assignments/team_members/teams on every
request; a single indexed point-lookup on token_version still gives
immediate revocation (token_version is bumped, individually or
cascaded to a team's current members, on any RoleAssignment/team
membership change, deactivation, or password change). Both grant
types on POST /v1/auth/token always recompute roles/tv fresh so a
refresh after invalidation reflects current permissions. Adds
users.token_version to log-server-storage and updates
log-server-auth/log-server-rbac accordingly.

commit.message:
Auth: revoke sessions on role/password/active changes; role from DB

RequireAuth now takes the caller's role from the DB (cached in authState
alongside is_active/token_version) instead of the JWT claim, and every
change that should end existing sessions bumps token_version: role change
or Admin password reset or deactivation via PUT /users/:id, bulk
deactivate, Delete, and ChangePassword. ChangePassword returns a fresh
token as data.access_token next to the user fields so the caller stays
signed in.

Also: user Create/Update reject an empty or unknown role with 422; Create
with status "inactive" now actually stores is_active false
(CreateKeepingFalse); Login checks the password before reporting
"Account is inactive".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Refresh sessions on role change instead of signing people out

Role grants and revokes, role-request approvals, claim approvals and
revokes, and moving someone to another org all bumped token_version.
That's the hard revoke, so it 401'd every device the person had: a diver
whose judge request got approved was thrown to the login page on their
phone and laptop. Since sessions now last until Sign out, that was the
last way people got logged out without asking to be.

Migration 106 adds users.claims_version and those paths bump it instead
(bumpClaimsVersion). The JWT carries it as cv. When verifyToken or
optionalAuth see a cv behind the row, they rebuild the claims from the DB
for this request and plant a fresh cookie, so a grant works and a revoke
bites on the very next request, with no sign-in. Bearer callers get the
fresh claims per request and no cookie. A tv bump racing the rebuild is
still a revoke, and a DB error is a 503, never a 401.

Sockets get the same treatment: the handshake rebuilds stale claims
(sessionClaimsForSocket, native tickets carry cv), and the per-event
re-check refreshes the socket's roles in place (refreshSocketSession),
moving its org / sysadmins rooms to match, so a revoked referee is
refused by the role check rather than disconnected.

The SPA watches for X-DivingHQ-Session: refreshed and reloads its
identity, so new nav shows up without a reload. /api/auth/me now answers
503 instead of 401 when it couldn't check the session, which used to
sign people out over a DB blip.

token_version stays for what should end sessions: password and 2FA
changes, suspension, deletion, a DOB correction.

Co-Authored-By: WOZCODE <contact@withwoz.com>

feat(auth): revoke access tokens before they expire (#70)

* feat(auth): revoke access tokens before they expire

Access tokens now carry a unique id (jti) and the user's token_version,
both checked on every request through the role cache, so a token can be
refused before it expires. This is the roadmap's jti denylist, and it lifts
the ~15 minute ceiling on JWT_EXPIRY_MINUTES.

- Logout revokes the access token sent with it, by jti, until it expires.
  The request stays unauthenticated: a missing, invalid or expired bearer
  token is ignored.
- Bumping token_version ends every session at once, on a password change,
  a deactivation, an account deletion and a replayed refresh token (which
  already revoked the refresh family, and now the access tokens too).
- Deactivating a member keeps their tokens revoked if they are reactivated.
- The hourly cleanup loop also drops revocations of tokens that would have
  expired anyway.

Revocation applies on the next request on the instance that handled it and
within the 30s role-cache TTL on any other. Tokens issued before this
change carry neither claim and are refused, so clients refresh once.

exactly why the role cannot live there.

Two things live testing settled. Supabase's admin endpoint MERGES
app_metadata rather than replacing it, so the first version of revoke --
which rebuilt the object without the role key -- reported success and
changed nothing, leaving an ex-adjuster with employee access. Clearing has to
send role=null explicitly. Verified by minting a real token before and after:
'employee' then None, with provider and providers surviving both.

The account lookup pages through the admin list endpoint instead of reading
the first page, since there is no email filter and the naive version would
have started missing users once the project outgrew one page.

Sessions are revoked after any change, because an access token already in a
browser carries its old app_metadata until it expires -- otherwise a revoke
would not take effect for up to an hour.

Verified end to end against the live project: dry run, apply, idempotent
re-run, and the backend's own SupabaseAuth reading role='employee' back out
of a freshly signed token. Probe account deleted.

commit.message:
Implement immediate account revocation

Live authorization
* Check Redis role, active status, and version on protected requests
* Deny access when shared state is missing or unavailable

Forced logout
* Revoke sessions and advance versions after role, status, and password changes
* Reject old tokens and return affected users to login

Operations and verification
* Add a private Redis container and authorization-state recovery command
* Test revocation, outages, and token validation across services

Auth: server-side session revocation (immediate logout + role/password change)

Sessions were stateless HMAC cookies valid until their 12h expiry: logout only
cleared the cookie client-side and a role/password change didn't take effect
until re-login. Add a per-user token_version:
- users gains a token_version column (migrated on existing DBs). The cookie
  embeds it; currentSession() re-checks it against the DB on every request, so
  a mismatch rejects the token immediately.
- Logout, and UpsertUser on password/role change (incl. via the create-user
  CLI), bump token_version -> all of that user's outstanding cookies are
  revoked at once.

Hardening from an adversarial review of the change (4 confirmed low findings):
- Logout uses verifyIgnoringExpiry so an expired-but-authentic cookie still
  revokes sibling sessions; a bump failure is now logged, not silently dropped.
- SQLite opened with WAL + busy_timeout(5000) so the per-request token_version
  read never spuriously fails (SQLITE_BUSY) while the create-user CLI writes.
- tokenVersion distinguishes 'user deleted' (revoke) from a transient DB error;
  on a transient error currentSession fails OPEN (keeps a validly-signed session,
  logs it) so a DB blip can't mass-logout valid users. Real revocations are a
  successful query with a mismatched version and still take effect.

Tests: revocation, role-change revocation, deleted-user, expired-cookie logout.
Note: deploying this logs everyone out once (old cookies have no version).

Revoke mobile JWTs on logout, password change and password reset

Mobile tokens were valid for their full 30 days (plus the 7-day refresh
grace) no matter what: API logout only cleared the Rails session, and
changing or resetting a password left every existing device token working.

- users.token_version (default 0); User#revoke_mobile_tokens! bumps it
- JwtService embeds token_version in auth tokens and rejects any token
  whose claim doesn't match the user's current version, on both verify
  and refresh (shared via JwtService.user_for_auth_claims)
- Tokens issued before this change carry no claim and count as version 0,
  so existing sessions survive the deploy until the user revokes
- Bumped on: DELETE /api/v1/logout, AccountController#update_password /
  #set_password, PasswordResetsController#update
- Also fixes the hardcoded "< 6" check in PasswordResetsController that
  CON-57 missed (now 8)

schema.rb: only the new column and version stamp are committed. A full
dump would drop roles/time_entries/workload_sentiments tables that exist
in schema.rb without migrations on main - tracked separately.

Closes CON-55

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(auth): decide session validity in Postgres, not in JWT claims or Redis

Fixes two issues reported by Dream Security against v0.1.0:

1. /auth/refresh (and every API request) trusted the role baked into
   the JWT, so a demoted or disabled admin kept admin rights — via
   refresh rotation, indefinitely.
2. Token revocation lived only in Redis and failed open, so every
   logged-out token became valid again whenever Redis was unreachable.

Each request now loads role, active flag and token_version from the
users table and checks the token's jti against a new revoked_tokens
table (migration 005). Tokens no longer carry a role claim.

- token_version bump ends all sessions of a user: role change,
  deactivation, password change, refresh-token replay
- refresh rotation claims the old jti atomically; a replayed or
  concurrently reused refresh token ends the whole session family
- logout also revokes the refresh token when the client sends it
- PATCH /users/{u}/active lets admins offboard a user without SQL
- change-password returns a fresh token pair for the calling client
- frontend: transparent single-flight refresh on 401, logout sends the
  refresh token, enable/disable toggle in user management

Redis is no longer on the auth path, so a cache outage can neither
resurrect revoked tokens nor lock operators out (failing closed, as the
report suggested, would have done the latter).

Adds tests/integration: runs the real app against TimescaleDB when
TEST_DATABASE_URL is set (CI now provides a service container).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
security(P1-7): instant token revocation + refresh rotation

Add a token_version ('tv') claim to every access/refresh token on both
identities (staff + customer). get_current_user / get_current_customer
reject a token whose tv no longer matches the stored value, so a token can
be killed server-side the moment it should no longer be trusted.

revoke_tokens() bumps the version on:
  - logout (staff + customer)  <- closes the A7 'logout only clears the
    client' gap: the Bearer token is dead immediately, not at expiry
  - self change-password / OTP reset-password (re-issues for the current
    session, kills all others)
  - admin reset-password, deactivate, and role change (kills the target's
    live sessions at once -> B8)

/auth/refresh and /client/auth/refresh now rotate: each call issues a fresh
access AND refresh token and checks tv (rejects a revoked family with 401).

Role/permissions are already read fresh from the DB every request, so a
role change is authoritative immediately; the tv bump additionally drops
any in-flight elevated session.

Verified end-to-end against Postgres (28/28 checks): staff logout ->
token 401; admin reset-password/deactivate/role-change -> target 401;
change-password -> old 401 / new 200; customer refresh rotates then
logout revokes both access + refresh.

Docs: MOBILE_SECURITY_STANDARDS A6 -> partial, A7/B8 -> done.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018WJoZH6UXjthewAHFzPoC8

feat(auth): JWT revocation via users.token_version (S4)

- migration m20260721_000008: users.token_version int not null default 0
- JWT claims carry tv (serde default: legacy tokens stay valid until bump)
- require_session_verified(): DB recheck for write paths (forum/comments/uploads)
- require_admin reuses same DB fetch for version check
- admin_set_user_role bumps version on role change (instant revoke)

security: revoke sessions when roles change

Advance users.token_version when grant_access changes a role so old privilege-bearing sessions are invalidated while repeated identical grants remain idempotent.

feat(auth): console sessions that can actually be revoked

A console JWT was believed on its own for its whole eight-hour life: the role
came out of the claims and the database was never asked, so disabling,
deleting or demoting an account changed nothing for the token already in that
person's browser, and there was no server-side logout at all.

Every request now verifies the signature and then reads the account row (two
primary-key lookups in api/services/sessions.py): the account must exist and be
enabled, its token_version must still match the token's new `ver` claim, and
the token's `jti` must not be on the logout denylist. The role that reaches the
request is the one in the table, so a demotion applies immediately; the claim
is still parsed, so a token naming a role that does not exist is refused as
before.

Migration 0038 adds users.token_version and revoked_tokens. New routes:
POST /api/auth/logout (this session), POST /api/auth/sessions/revoke-all (your
account, everywhere) and POST /api/users/{username}/sessions/revoke-all
(platform admin). Password, role and disable/enable writes bump the version in
the same transaction that makes the change.

Key rotation stops being a fleet-wide logout: OCTO_JWT_SECRET_PREVIOUS lists
retired keys that are still verified while their tokens expire, nothing is ever
signed with one, and a `kid` header names the signing key so the verifier tries
that one rather than each in turn. While OCTO_AGENT_JWT_SECRET is unset the
agent key is derived from the operator key, so the same list rotates both
audiences; OCTO_AGENT_JWT_SECRET_PREVIOUS covers the explicit case.

Tokens minted before this carry no `ver` and keep working until they expire —
the migration backfills every account at generation 0, which is what those
tokens implicitly claim. Signing the whole console out mid-rollout was the
worse default; an operator who wants it runs revoke-all afterwards.

The console warns five minutes before a session ends and calls the logout
endpoint on sign-out. Refresh tokens, a shorter access lifetime and an idle
timeout are still open on the issue.

Refs #314

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(identity): [protected] reset links, password change and required change (BPMS-021, OQ-15)

Account recovery as decided in docs/06 §3.6.1 and docs/22 A-39.

- Migration 0036: password_resets (system scope like users and
  refresh_tokens; token stored only as SHA-256), users.must_change_password,
  and member:security.manage on the built-in owner/admin roles of existing
  workspaces (per-workspace scope under forced RLS).
- request_password_reset: always Ok; 32-byte single-use links valid 30
  minutes, a newer request voids older ones, 3 self-service requests per
  account per hour; unknown, inactive and rate-limited requests return
  nothing to send. Audited password.reset_requested either way.
- check_reset_token, reset_password (policy applies, every session and
  refresh token revoked, token version bumped, second factors kept;
  password.reset).
- change_password: the current password is checked and failures count
  toward the sign-in lockout; other sessions are revoked and the current one
  continues with a re-signed access token (password.changed).
- Sign-in returns PasswordChangeRequired with a 10-minute pwchange token
  bound to the token version (so single use) when an admin required a
  change; complete_expired_change sets the password and continues to
  two-step verification as a password sign-in would.
- revoke_all_sessions(user, by, reason) with the actor recorded;
  revoke_all delegates to it.

Tests follow in the next commits (identity DB tests, audit contract).
